S63.01.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan (the create controls are hidden otherwise) and at least one existing routine, because the gallery panel only shows when the list is not empty
S63.01.note: The gallery panel is rendered only when galleryOpen is true and the routine list is not empty; with no routines the empty state shows Create Your First Schedule instead. Whether the gallery can be reopened at any time was not confirmed.
steps: Click Scheduled in the sidebar.
Click the chevron beside New task (its label is More ways to create a task).
Click Start from a template.
Look for the Start from a template panel with a grid labelled Schedule templates, and check you can browse several templates.
S63.01.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > More ways to create a task (chevron beside New task) > Start from a template

S63.02.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan; a Free account sees Scheduled tasks are available on Basic and higher plans.
S63.02.note: The earlier in-app check was blocked by plan (E054), so creation was not exercised.
steps: Click Scheduled in the sidebar.
Click New task, or choose Create from scratch from the chevron menu.
In the Create Schedule dialog, type your instructions in Task Instructions and enter a Schedule Name.
Click Create Schedule and check that the new routine appears in the list with its name and prompt.
S63.02.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch, then fill Task Instructions and click Create Schedule

S63.03.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and a finished chat reply
S63.03.note: The menu's trigger button text was not confirmed; only the menu item label was found.
steps: Open a chat and wait for an assistant reply to finish.
Open the more-actions menu on that reply (its trigger label was not confirmed in code).
Click Run this on a schedule.
Check that the Create Schedule dialog opens pre-filled from that reply, then save it and look for the new routine under Scheduled.
S63.03.where: Chat > an assistant reply's more-actions menu > Run this on a schedule

S63.04.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Type a value in Schedule Name and an optional value in Description.
Click Create Schedule.
Click the edit (pencil) button on the routine, change Schedule Name or Description, click Save Changes, and check the card shows the new values.
S63.04.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch (Schedule Name and Description fields); to edit later, Scheduled > Edit <routine name>

S63.05.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Type several lines in Task Instructions, including a line break.
Click Create Schedule, then open the routine's edit (pencil) button.
Check that the Task Instructions text is shown and editable, and that Save Changes stores the change.
S63.05.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch (Task Instructions box); edit later with Scheduled > Edit <routine name>

S63.06.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan; a project may be needed for project-file sources (the code passes a hasProject flag)
S63.06.note: Which source options appear depends on whether a project is selected; the exact option labels were not extracted.
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Find the Sources group in the form.
Tick and untick the source options offered.
Click Create Schedule and open Edit on the routine to check the same sources are still ticked.
S63.06.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Sources

S63.08.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and at least one connected connector account to see options
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Find the Connectors group in the form; wait for Reading your connectors… to finish.
Tick the connectors the run may use and untick others.
Click Create Schedule and reopen Edit to check the selection is kept.
S63.08.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Connectors

S63.09.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and at least one custom agent; the field appears only when agents exist
S63.09.note: The field is hidden when no agent options exist.
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Open the Run as agent dropdown.
Choose an agent and read the description that appears under it.
Click Create Schedule, then check the routine card or Edit dialog shows the chosen agent.
S63.09.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Run as agent

S63.11.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan
S63.11.note: The earlier in-app check was blocked by plan (E054).
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Set Frequency to One Time.
Set Run At to a future date and time.
Click Create Schedule and check the card's Next Run shows that time.
S63.11.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Frequency > One Time, then Run At

S63.12.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan; a long wait is needed to see a scheduled fire
S63.12.note: The firing itself is a server cron route (apps/web/app/api/cron/run-schedules/route.ts) with no screen; the tester sees it through Next Run and Last Run.
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Set Frequency to Daily, Weekly or Monthly, and set Repeat Every where shown.
Click Create Schedule and read the Next Run value on the card.
Wait for a due time, or use Run now, then check Last Run and the run history update.
S63.12.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Frequency > Daily (or Weekly, Monthly, Interval)

S63.13.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan
S63.13.note: Suggestions come from a datalist; the helper text says daylight saving follows the chosen zone.
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Click Time Zone and type a city or region such as the zone you want.
Pick a zone from the suggestions, set a time, and click Create Schedule.
Open the routine card and compare the Time Zone and Next Run values with the zone you chose.
S63.13.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Time Zone

S63.14.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan
S63.14.note: The Recurrence Rule field was located but its inner behaviour was not read; run windows are the Only Run During setting.
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Open Frequency and choose Custom Cron, then type a value in Cron Expression.
Try Recurrence Rule, then Interval with Repeat Every.
Open When It May Run, And What Happens If It Fails and set Only Run During; then check each saved routine's Next Run and Timing.
S63.14.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Frequency > Custom Cron, Recurrence Rule or Interval; Only Run During is under When It May Run, And What Happens If It Fails

S63.15.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan, the matching connector account for the source, and an outside account for the event source
S63.15.note: A trigger is added from the routine card, not from the create form; the Frequency option When An Event Happens is the form-side choice.
steps: Click Scheduled and open a routine with the History button (title Run History).
Scroll to the Triggers for section and click Add trigger.
Choose a source such as Gmail, GitHub, Slack or Google Calendar, then fill its fields and click Add trigger to save.
Send or simulate an event from that source and check the routine appears in its run history.
S63.15.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > routine card > History button (title Run History) > Triggers for <routine name> > Add trigger

S63.16.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and an event source connected to send events
steps: Open a routine's History (title Run History) and click Add trigger.
Set Event types and the Ignore repeats for (seconds) value.
Under Only when, add a condition: pick a field, a comparison and a value.
Save the trigger, then send an event that matches and one that does not, and check only the matching one starts a run.
S63.16.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > routine card > History button > Triggers for <routine name> > Add trigger > Only when and Event types

S63.17.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan, a command-line tool or script that can sign a POST (the panel shows an openssl example)
S63.17.note: The secret is shown in the panel after creation; its exact on-screen text was not found.
steps: Open a routine's History (title Run History), click Add trigger.
Choose Anything else (signed webhook) and click Add trigger to save.
Copy the URL and signing secret shown after saving (the exact display text was not extracted).
Send a signed POST to the URL and check a run starts; then click Regenerate secret and check the old secret is rejected.
S63.17.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > routine card > History button > Triggers for <routine name> > Add trigger > Anything else (signed webhook)

S63.19.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan
S63.19.note: Run now is disabled when canRun is false; the conditions were not traced.
steps: Click Scheduled and open the More actions menu on a routine card.
Click Run now.
Wait for the run to finish, then open the History button (title Run History).
Check the newest run in the list shows a status and open View Output to see the result.
S63.19.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > More actions for <routine name> > Run now

S63.20.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and a routine that has a future run
steps: Click Scheduled and find a routine card.
Read the Next Run row and the Timing row.
Compare the next-run time with the routine's Time Zone row.
Use Edit to change the timing, save, and check Next Run changes.
S63.20.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > each routine card (Next Run row)

S63.21.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and a routine that has run at least once, ideally one that failed
S63.21.note: Whether the card row itself shows a failure, or only the history does, was not confirmed.
steps: Click Scheduled and find a routine that has run.
Read the Last Run row.
Open History (title Run History) and check the latest run's status badge.
Compare the failed status shown there with Last Run.
S63.21.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > each routine card (Last Run row)

S63.22.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and a routine with past runs
steps: Click Scheduled and click the History button on a routine (its aria label is View History for <name>).
Read the Run History heading and the list of runs.
Check each row's status badge and time.
Click Load more if it appears and check older runs load.
S63.22.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > History button (title Run History) on a routine card

S63.23.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and a run that produced output
S63.23.note: View Output appears only when the run has result text; latest result also opens from a separate card control.
steps: Open a routine's History (title Run History).
Click a run row's View Output disclosure.
Read the output text under it.
Compare the text with the run's status and time shown on the row.
S63.23.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > History button > a run row > View Output

S63.24.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan
S63.24.note: The switch has no visible text; its accessible name is Pause <name> or Resume <name>.
steps: Click Scheduled and find a routine card.
Click its switch to pause, which turns the card to Paused.
Read the message that appears (Schedule paused.).
Click the switch again to resume and check the card no longer shows Paused and the message is Schedule resumed.
S63.24.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > the switch on a routine card (pause or resume)

S63.26.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and an existing routine
steps: Click Scheduled and click the Edit button on a routine card.
In the Edit Schedule dialog, change Schedule Name, a timing field or Task Instructions.
Click Save Changes.
Check the dialog closes, the message Schedule updated. appears and the card shows the new values.
S63.26.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > Edit <routine name> (pencil button, title Edit Schedule)

S63.27.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and an existing routine
S63.27.note: The confirm button's exact text was not extracted.
steps: Click Scheduled and open the More actions menu on a routine card.
Click Delete.
Read the Delete Schedule? confirmation and click the confirm button.
Check the routine disappears from the list and no longer shows a next run.
S63.27.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > More actions for <routine name> > Delete

S63.29.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and a second account or private window to view the shared link
S63.29.note: The share dialog title is built from the routine name; the copy button label and how a recipient makes their own copy were not found in the read files.
steps: Click Scheduled and open the More actions menu on a routine card.
Click Share.
In the Share dialog, create the share link and copy it.
Open the link in a private window or as a second account and check a preview of the routine is shown (its copy action was not found).
S63.29.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > More actions for <routine name> > Share

S63.31.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and enough credits to reach the cap
S63.31.note: The cap pauses the routine after current credits are used; a run already started finishes (helper text in the form).
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Open the Execution Limits section and enter a value in Credit Cap or Maximum Runs.
Click Create Schedule and open Edit on the routine to check the value is kept.
Run the routine until the cap is reached and check it pauses once runs use the credits.
S63.31.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Execution Limits > Credit Cap (or Maximum Runs)

S63.32.needs: a schedule whose run needs a tool approval (for example one that uses a tool requiring approval)
S63.32.note: The approval card and Approve/Deny buttons are in code, and the resume path is in apps/web/features/schedules/components/SchedulesPage.tsx; the approval pause itself is server-side (scheduled-agent-executor.ts), so whether a real run pauses and resumes was not checked. The card title and Approve label are confirmed in code; the "Approved." message is built from SchedulesPage.tsx and the outcome text varies.
steps: Sign in and click "Scheduled" in the sidebar.
Find a schedule whose run needs a tool approval. Its card may show a paused note: "Paused: a run needed your approval. Approve or deny it in Run History".
Click the Run History icon on that schedule's card (title "Run History").
In the run list, find the run with the "Waiting for your approval" card and read the tool name listed under it.
Click "Approve" (or "Deny") on that card.
Check that the run continues and the status changes from waiting to a finished state, and that a message says "Approved." appeared.
S63.32.where: Scheduled > (open a schedule's card) > Run History (the clock icon, title "Run History") > run row showing "Waiting for your approval" > Approve

S63.33.needs: a schedule that has a missed or skipped run (for example a schedule set to skip missed runs whose run was late)
S63.33.note: The note text is built in packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/schedules.ts (for example "Skipped the run scheduled for ...: it was missed by ... and this schedule skips missed runs." and "Ran late: scheduled for ..."), so the exact note is dynamic and not a fixed label; the missed-run detection is in apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts. Whether a real run is marked missed was not checked.
steps: Sign in and click "Scheduled" in the sidebar.
Find a schedule that has a run marked as missed or skipped. A schedule with missed runs set to skip shows these.
Click the Run History icon on that schedule's card (title "Run History").
Find the run row. Its status word is "skipped" when the run was skipped.
Read the grey note under the run row. It says the run was skipped, the scheduled time, and how late it was.
Compare the note and status with Expected: the history should say that a run was missed or skipped and why.
S63.33.where: Scheduled > (open a schedule's card) > Run History (the clock icon, title "Run History") > run row with the "skipped" status and a note above it
